# The Geriatrician's Guide

> Independent guidance on senior care decisions, written by Michael D. Genualdi, MD, a Stanford-trained physician board-certified in geriatrics and internal medicine. The Geriatrician's Guide takes no money from senior living communities: no referral fees, no placement commissions, no operator sponsorships.

The site publishes educational content for people making care decisions for an older adult. Topics include recognizing when living at home is no longer safe, the levels of care, what senior care costs and how Medicare, Medicaid, long-term care insurance, and veterans benefits pay for it, how to tour and evaluate a senior living community, staying involved after move-in, dementia care, and end-of-life planning.

Content is written for a US audience. Where a program or rule varies by state, it is identified as state-specific.

All content is general education. It is not medical, legal, or financial advice, and reading it does not create a physician-patient relationship. Patient stories are de-identified composites.

## About

- [About Dr. Genualdi](https://www.geriatriciansguide.com/about): The author's clinical background and training, and why the guide accepts no industry money.

## The book

- [The Long Road](https://www.geriatriciansguide.com/the-long-road): *The Long Road: A Geriatrician's Complete Guide to Senior Care Decisions*. Forty-one chapters in six parts: Before the Decision; The Financial Picture; Choosing Well: Touring, Evaluating, and Deciding; After Move-In: Staying Involved; Dementia: Understanding, Caring, and Deciding; The End of Life. Digital edition, $97, sold directly.

## Articles

- [Articles](https://www.geriatriciansguide.com/blog): Physician-written articles on senior care costs, insurance coverage, levels of care, community evaluation, dementia, and end-of-life planning.
